title: June 2024: the Finance Bill protests
text: Young people led protests against the Finance Bill in June 2024, and demonstrators entered Parliament's grounds. The national rights commission (KNCHR) counts 63 or more deaths, 610 injuries and 74 enforced disappearances in the 2024 protests, with 26 people still unaccounted for; Amnesty International counts at least 60 killed.
caveat: The counts differ by source, rights groups say they may be higher, and the article does not reconcile them.

title: June and July 2025: the anniversary and 7 July marches
text: Marches on 25 June and 7 July 2025 ended in many deaths. For 25 June the KNCHR counts 19 deaths and 531 injuries and the police oversight authority (IPOA) counts 195 injuries; for 7 July the KNCHR counts 38 deaths and IPOA 146 injuries. IPOA recorded 65 deaths for June and July 2025 together.
source: Amnesty Kenya and OdipoDev, Freedom Index half-year 2026 report, 10 August 2026
caveat: The report prints the two bodies' counts without reconciling them, so they should not be added; earlier published counts for both dates were lower.

title: Two years on: prosecutions and compensation
text: The police oversight authority (IPOA) said on 22 June 2026 that only 3 of 62 deaths are before the courts and 46 are still being investigated. The state has begun compensating victims of protest violence from 2013 to 2025: the first phase covers 348 confirmed victims, including families of 115 people killed.
caveat: Families say payment cannot replace accountability. Taking part in the compensation scheme is voluntary.

title: Young Kenyans and the 2027 vote: a small survey
text: A study of 531 people aged 18 to 29 in 19 counties, by OdipoDev and Tribeless Youth, found that at least seven in ten plan to vote in 2027. It names registering to vote and distrust of the electoral commission as the main obstacles, and says that since the 2024 protests young people feel a firmer duty to vote.
caveat: Respondents were reached by street intercepts and field surveys, so this is not a national estimate; a plan to vote is not turnout.

title: Half of Kenyans doubted the 2027 elections' integrity
text: A poll in May 2025, cited in an analysis of young voters, found that half of Kenyans had no confidence at all in the integrity of the 2027 elections. The analysis argues that young people's distrust of the system, more than apathy, explains why many stayed off the register before 2024.
source: Africa Is a Country, "Gen Z's electoral dilemma", February 2026
caveat: Second-hand: the article does not name the pollster, and it is an opinion and analysis piece.

title: Nairobi leads the 2026 registration drive
text: In the IEBC's month-long mass registration drive, which ended on 28 April 2026, Nairobi registered the most new voters, 276,886 of the drive's 2,345,476, ahead of Kiambu with 128,859 and Nakuru with 102,207. The paper printed figures for 17 counties.
caveat: The figures are for the mass drive only and not final: the register is still to be cleaned, verified and audited.

title: 2,612,725 new registrations since September 2025
text: The IEBC's drive ended in April 2026 with 2,612,725 new voters: 2,345,476 in the enhanced drive and 267,249 through continuous registration at its offices since 29 September 2025. The commission gave no age or gender breakdown, but said many registrants were young, partly because some centres were at tertiary institutions.
caveat: Gross figures: duplicates and errors are still to be removed and an audited register gazetted. Registration continues.

title: How many of the new registrants are young
text: An IEBC commissioner, Anne Nderitu, said on 5 May 2026 that the commission believes young people are more than half of the new registrants, against about 40% of the register in 2022.
caveat: A belief, not a published count: no age breakdown has been released and the article does not say what ages count as young.

title: Young voters in the 2022 register
text: In the 2022 register 8,811,693 voters were aged 18 to 34, about 39.8% of it, and 5.4 million were aged 18 to 29.
caveat: National figures for the whole 2022 register; none is given for Nairobi.

title: 2025: young people's protests around the world
text: In 2025 protests led by young people in Indonesia, Nepal, Madagascar, Morocco and Peru denounced corruption, inequality and political exclusion, and asked for schools, health care and housing. In Nepal the government fell and an interim prime minister was chosen; in Madagascar the president was removed in a military takeover; in Morocco the cabinet announced reforms and spending on schools and hospitals. Deaths were reported in four of the five.
caveat: Outcomes differ widely and the article does not cover Kenya; how far the movement bears on Kenya's 2027 vote is for the reader to judge.

title: 15 October 2025: Raila Odinga dies
text: Raila Odinga died on 15 October 2025. An analysis argues that his death removed the opposition's most reliable organiser and sharpened a split inside ODM between members who oppose the government's policies and a faction that works with it.
source: Africa Is a Country, "Gen Z's electoral dilemma", February 2026

title: 12 July 2026: ODM says it will back President Ruto
text: ODM leader Oburu Oginga said in Homa Bay that ODM will not field a presidential candidate in 2027 and will support President Ruto for a second term. The report says nothing about ODM's choices for governor or Senate seats.
caveat: A statement of intent: it does not say how ODM members, voters or the party's county branches will act.

title: September 2025: an impeachment motion is shelved
text: In early September 2025 Nairobi's MCAs shelved a motion to impeach Governor Johnson Sakaja, after President Ruto urged UDA members of the county assembly to drop it and Raila Odinga met ODM's lawmakers and MCAs. Insiders put the pause at at least a month.
caveat: The motion was suspended, not withdrawn. The article does not say what the grievances were, and other reports give the length of the pause as 30 days to two months.

title: A May 2026 poll with the incumbent first
text: A Darubini Research poll fielded on 16 and 19 May 2026 by household face-to-face interviews, with 500 adults targeted in each county, had Governor Johnson Sakaja on 48%, James Gakuya on 28% and Babu Owino on 17% in the Nairobi governor race.
caveat: No margin of error and no completed sample are reported; the three figures add to 93%, which the article does not explain, and it gives no figure for Agnes Kagure. The polls in this race disagree widely, so none is a share of the 2027 vote.

title: A July 2026 poll with the incumbent far behind
text: A Centre for African Progress poll fielded from 11 to 16 July 2026 among 4,500 people in Nairobi's 17 constituencies and 85 wards, face to face, had Babu Owino on 36%, Agnes Kagure on 32%, Governor Sakaja on 11%, Milton Lucheri on 10% and James Gakuya on 7%, with 4% undecided.
source: Citizen Digital, 25 July 2026 (Centre for African Progress)
caveat: No margin of error is reported. The polls in this race disagree widely, so none is a share of the 2027 vote.

title: An August 2026 poll with two challengers close
text: A Mizani Africa poll fielded from 21 to 28 August 2026 among 1,820 registered voters across Nairobi's 17 constituencies (margin of error 2.3 points) had Babu Owino on 28.4%, Agnes Kagure on 27.2%, Governor Sakaja on 17.0% and James Gakuya on 15.0%, with 8.1% undecided.
caveat: The article does not say how respondents were reached, and its figures leave 4.3% unaccounted for. The polls in this race disagree widely, including on the incumbent (11% in one, 17% in this one, 48% in another), so none is a share of the 2027 vote.

title: Babu Owino: prepared to run for governor
text: Embakasi East MP Babu Owino said on 15 September 2026 that he backs Senator Edwin Sifuna for president and is prepared to run for Nairobi governor in 2027. He said he would put more time into organising in Nairobi, which he described as 85 wards and about 2.5 million registered voters.
caveat: The article names no party for him and does not say whether the Linda Mwananchi movement it mentions is a registered party.

title: Babu Owino: a party of his own, not ODM's ticket
text: Babu Owino told Citizen Digital that he already has a registered party of his own, set up before the Linda Mwananchi movement, and implied he will run for Nairobi governor on it: he said ODM would not let him run, so he formed a party, after ODM leaders backed Governor Sakaja for another term at an event at Bomas in February 2025. He backs Sifuna for president and said Sifuna accepted a coalition in which Sifuna leads and he leads his own party.
caveat: The article does not name the party or say outright which ticket he will use. That ODM leaders backed Sakaja is his account; the article carries no statement from ODM.

title: Winnie Odinga announces a bid for the Nairobi Senate seat
text: Winnie Odinga, a member of the East African Legislative Assembly, announced at an event marking a year since her father Raila Odinga's death that she will run for Nairobi's Senate seat in 2027. She said she wants more young people in leadership and that many people have lost hope after studying, looking for work and voting without seeing progress.
caveat: The article names no party or coalition and does not discuss the governor's race. It says the senator now, Edwin Sifuna, is seeking higher office without saying which.
